note: The garden scene turns on a verbatim scripture quotation — the passage Augustine's eye fell on in Romans 13 — so it is the one place in these five bios where getting the Bible text exactly right decides whether the paragraph works. Both it and the line Alypius applied to himself (Romans 14:1) are IRV byte-for-byte.

«Tolle, lege» is left in Latin, as the English leaves it, with the Hindi rendering following it in the same sentence — the child's chant is a Latin artefact of the story, not a phrase to translate away.
Everything else quoted is Augustine's own (the Confessions, Monica's words, Possidius's record), so there is nothing further to mine.

Take Root API is egress-blocked from this container (curl to api.takeroot.bible returns 000). The IRV text was fetched instead from the ebible mirror on raw.githubusercontent.com (gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/hin_irv/usx — note the collection serves USX, not USFM), all 66 books / 31,104 verses, and every span marked mined was lifted from it with a script rather than typed.

The eight already-shipped Hindi bios MIRROR their English source's quotation marks — 8 of 8 pairs, including frederick-brotherton-meyer, whose English uses 18 straight quotes and whose Hindi carries exactly 18. Measured as PAIRS rather than as a column, which is what stops meyer looking like an outlier. This bio mirrors its own source accordingly.

Reconciled against the shipped Hindi corpus before shipping: conversion is मन-फिराव, the term the eight shipped bios settled on (9 uses, and zero of the मन-परिवर्तन this run first wrote). Names follow the shipped forms — डी. एल. मूडी, and हडसन टेलर as the Hindi deeper-life-in-christ plan card (job #696) fixed it.
